Findings of the WMT’22 Shared Task on Large-Scale Machine Translation Evaluation for African Languages

paper.acl.2022.wmt-1.72

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at ACL-Anthology-2022.wmt-1.72-captured-2026-11-10. Human translation evaluation construction, annotator normalization and restricted available language-pair subset are substantive primary methods, not abstract-only evidence. No all100-pair human coverage inferred. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Human-score averages cover a smaller annotator-available subset of the 100 evaluation pairs; the paper also notes that the previous year used the FLORES-101 sentencepiece tokenizer while this year used FLORES-200.

Human evaluators scored two system translations per source sentence on a 0–100 scale combining accuracy and fluency, with annotator-level Z-score normalization.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Human evaluation ran on Toloka with Africa-IP and declared-language filters, English/French platform language tests when available, five-item exams, and bans after repeated very fast submissions; non-English/French exam pass threshold was 80%, compared with 100% when a platform language test was available.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Across the 72 language pairs comparable with the previous shared task, the reported average BLEU increased from 15.09 to 22.60, about 7.5 points, with 67 pairs improving.
